title: Asset Purchase Agreement: Willowmere Court Assisted Living and Memory Care (residential care facility for the elderly)
fictional_notice: All parties and facts are invented.

defects.title: Property and business transfer at closing before the buyer is licensed
defects.why: Licensing is expressly not a closing condition, and the real property and business pass to the buyer even if its application is still pending, with the buyer operating under the seller's license. The property and business may not be transferred until the buyer qualifies for a license or provisional license.
quotes: If the License Application remains pending on the Closing Date, title to the Real Property and the Business shall nonetheless transfer to Buyer at the Closing, and Buyer shall operate the Community under the Existing License until Buyer's own license is issued.

defects.title: License application due 45 days after the due diligence period ends
defects.why: The buyer has until 45 days after the due diligence period expires, which is about 75 days after signing and after the scheduled closing, to file its license application. The buyer must apply for a license within five days of the seller's acceptance of the offer.
quotes: Buyer shall prepare and file with the Department a complete License Application not later than forty-five (45) days after the expiration of the Due Diligence Period.

defects.title: Residents notified only 10 days before closing
defects.why: Written notice to each resident or legal representative is due only 10 days before the closing. On a sale that results in a new license, the licensee must give that notice at least 30 days before the transfer, or when a bona fide offer is made, whichever period is longer.
quotes: Seller shall deliver written notice of the sale to each resident of the Community or the resident's legal representative not later than ten (10) days prior to the Closing Date, in a form reasonably approved by Buyer.

defects.title: Department of Social Services notified only 7 days before closing
defects.why: The communications protocol has the seller notify the Department of the proposed sale seven days before closing. The licensee must give written notice to the Department at least 30 days before the transfer, or when a bona fide offer is made, whichever period is longer.
quotes: Seller shall deliver written notice of the proposed sale to the Department not later than seven (7) days prior to the Closing Date

defects.title: All 92 community employees terminated at closing on 14 days' notice
defects.why: The seller must terminate every employee as of the closing date on 14 days' notice, and the buyer has no duty to hire any of them. The community has had at least 85 employees over the prior 12 months, so a mass layoff or termination requires 60 days' written notice.
quotes: Seller shall terminate all Community Employees effective as of the Closing Date, and shall give each Community Employee written notice of termination at least fourteen (14) days before the Closing Date.

defects.title: Eighteen-month noncompete imposed on two employees who own no interest in the seller
defects.why: The executive director and memory care program director, who are employees with no membership interest in the seller, must agree to an 18-month, 25-mile noncompete as a condition of being hired by the buyer. They are not selling goodwill or an ownership interest, so no exception applies and requiring the covenant is unlawful.
quotes: As a condition of any offer of employment by Buyer, the Executive Director and the Memory Care Program Director, who are employees and hold no membership interest in Seller, shall each agree that for eighteen (18) months after separation from Buyer for any reason he or she will not work for any assisted living or memory care community within twenty-five (25) miles of the Community.

defects.title: Buyer waives tax clearance certificate and withholds nothing for sales and use tax
defects.why: The buyer waives the tax clearance certificate and agrees that nothing will be withheld from the price for the seller's sales or use tax, although the seller holds a seller's permit. A buyer who does not withhold until the seller produces a receipt or certificate becomes personally liable for the seller's unpaid tax up to the purchase price.
quotes: Buyer waives any requirement that Seller obtain a tax clearance certificate from the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, and no portion of the Purchase Price shall be withheld at the Closing on account of any sales or use tax liability of Seller.
